newsitem.title: USA: May Department November sales rise.
newsitem.headline: May Department November sales rise.

text.p: May Department Stores Co said Thursday that November same store sales rose 6.9 percent.
Total sales for the month gained 12.9 percent to $1.13 billion from $1.0 billion.
It said November sales benefited from the inclusion of the Thanksgiving holiday, which falls five days closer to Christmas in 1996 than in 1995.
Sales for the first 10 months of fiscal 1996 were $8.77 billion, up 11.7 percent from $7.85 billion a year ago. On a comparable store basis, sales rose 4.6 percent.

May said sales were restated to exclude stores that have been closed and not replaced. Year-to-date revenues, including sales of non-replaced stores and finance charge revenues were $9.06 billion in 1996 and $8.14 billion in 1995.
May said it opened four new stores in November. Year-to-date, it opened a total of 28 department stores, including 13 acquired locations. This completes the planned store openings for 1996, May said.
May operates 365 department stores in 30 states and the District of Columbia.
